blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At the intermediate level, tax vocabulary stops being a list of words and becomes a working language. A meeting with an external advisor, a letter to the tax office, a clarification email to a colleague — each one depends on using the right word at the right moment. Exemption, deduction, allowance, relief, credit, rebate: each has a precise meaning, and mixing them up quietly damages your credibility.

The distinctions matter. A deduction reduces taxable income. A credit reduces the tax itself. A rebate is a refund after tax has been paid. An allowance is a specific amount the law lets you not count. These distinctions are easy to learn with practice, and impossible to fake in a room full of people who know them.

Speaking the language well does not make you a tax expert. But it does mean the tax experts in the room start taking you seriously — which is usually where the real work begins.

items.q: According to the text, what does mixing up tax words quietly damage?
items.why: "mixing them up quietly damages your credibility" — usar o termo errado corrói a confiança em você.

items.q: According to the text, what does a credit reduce?
items.why: "A credit reduces the tax itself" — diferente da dedução, que reduz a renda tributável.

items.q: What is a rebate, according to the text?
options: A refund after tax has been paid
A discount offered by an advisor
A specific amount you may not count
items.why: "A rebate is a refund after tax has been paid."

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Using the wrong tax term can cost you credibility.
Precise language earns you a seat at serious conversations.
Deduction and credit are not interchangeable.
You can bluff your way through a room of specialists if you sound confident.
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz que essas distinções são "impossible to fake" diante de quem conhece — blefar não funciona.

items.q: What does the final line suggest about speaking the language well?
options: It is the end of the process
It replaces the need for tax advisors
It is a starting point, not the whole job
It guarantees a lower tax bill
items.why: Inferência: "which is usually where the real work begins" — falar bem abre a porta; o trabalho de verdade vem depois.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Harry orientando um colega novo. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Can I grab you for two minutes before you send that? I noticed something in the last few emails, and I'd rather flag it now than let it snowball.

You've been using 'deduction' and 'credit' as if they were the same thing. They're not, and the advisor picked up on it in yesterday's call. A deduction reduces the income we're taxed on. A credit comes off the tax bill itself, pound for pound. So when you wrote that the R&D scheme would 'deduct' fifty thousand from what we owe, that's actually a credit — and the number the advisor quoted back was wrong because of it.

Honestly, it's a small thing, but with an external advisor these small things add up. If we're loose with the words, they start double-checking everything we say, and that slows the whole engagement down.

So here's what I'd suggest. Before anything goes out, ask yourself one question: is this reducing the income or reducing the tax? If it's the income, it's a deduction or an allowance. If it's the tax, it's a credit. Get that split right and you'll sound like you've been doing this for years.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Why did Harry stop his colleague before the email went out?
options: The email was sent to the wrong person
The advisor had complained about the tone
The numbers had not been approved yet
items.why: "You've been using 'deduction' and 'credit' as if they were the same thing. They're not."

items.q: According to Harry, how does a credit differ from a deduction?
options: A credit reduces the income; a deduction reduces the tax
A credit comes off the tax bill itself; a deduction reduces taxable income
There is no real difference between them
A credit is a refund; a deduction is an allowance
items.why: "A deduction reduces the income we're taxed on. A credit comes off the tax bill itself."

items.q: What was wrong with the colleague's line about the R&D scheme?
options: The fifty thousand figure was invented
It called a credit a 'deduction', so the advisor quoted a wrong number
The scheme did not qualify at all
It was sent before the deadline
items.why: "that's actually a credit — and the number the advisor quoted back was wrong because of it."

items.q: What does Harry imply happens when you are 'loose with the words'?
options: The tax office issues a fine
The advisor starts double-checking everything, slowing things down
The advisor charges a lower fee
items.why: Inferência: "they start double-checking everything we say, and that slows the whole engagement down."

items.q: How would you best describe Harry's approach with the colleague?
options: Corrective but supportive, offering a simple rule
items.why: Inferência: ele aponta o erro, mas dá uma regra prática ("is this reducing the income or the tax?") — tom de ajuda.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The export scheme qualifies for a full exemption, so no tax is due on those sales." An exemption is…
options: a small reduction in the tax rate
a refund paid after the tax year
a delay in the payment deadline
a release from having to pay a tax at all
items.why: Exemption = isenção: fica-se livre de pagar o tributo.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "We sent a short ___ to the advisor because two figures in the report seemed to contradict each other."
items.why: Clarification email = e-mail de esclarecimento, para resolver a contradição nos números.

items.q: "Each employee gets a travel allowance that is not counted as taxable income." Here, an allowance is…
options: a specific amount the rules let you not count
a percentage taken off the final tax
items.why: Allowance = abatimento: um valor específico que a lei permite não incluir na conta.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "After overpaying last quarter, the company received a ___ of eight thousand from the tax office."
items.why: Rebate = restituição: devolução depois de o imposto ter sido pago a mais.

items.q: "You can't fake the terminology in front of specialists." To fake something means to…
options: pretend to know or have it when you don't
items.why: To fake = fingir: aparentar domínio que não se tem.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem em conversas sobre impostos e reuniões com consultores. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The advisor picked up on the mistake straight away." To pick up on means to…
items.why: Pick up on = perceber, dar-se conta de algo.

items.q: "I'd rather flag this now than deal with it later." To flag something means to…
items.why: To flag = sinalizar, chamar a atenção para um ponto.

items.q: "With an external advisor, small errors add up." To add up here means to…
items.why: Add up = ir se acumulando até virar algo relevante.

items.q: "The finance director still has to sign off on the tax return before we file it." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "Getting the wording right won't move the needle on the tax we owe, but it protects our credibility." To move the needle means to…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, causar diferença perceptível (aqui, na conta do imposto).
